gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-andada-pro: Aaargh is a blunt, commanding display face whose bowls and stems all share one line width, and Andada Pro sits beneath it as a bookish serif. Shrink the heading and that heft fades fast.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-aref-ruqaa: Dignified and traditional, Aref Ruqaa is the serif doing the quiet work, with mild stroke variation and bowls that welcome the eye. And Aaargh above it, with horizontals as heavy as its verticals, keeps the page from sounding too hushed.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-aref-ruqaa-ink: Aaargh hits hard, its stroke widths holding firm from stem to curve with no thinning anywhere. Aref Ruqaa Ink, a classic serif, swells gently at the shoulders, and that softness is what makes the pairing work.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-average: Blunt headline, gentle text. Aaargh uses no thick-and-thin contrast at all, while Average, a text serif, brings the faint reed-pen thickening of a literary page, so paragraphs ease along without any stiffness.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-besley: Every stroke in Aaargh is a single unit width, joints and curves alike. It does bold and blunt best, whereas Besley, a classic serif, handles dignified editorial text with gentle weight shifts in its bowls.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-biz-udpmincho: BIZ UDPMincho reads as a refined classic serif, with mild thicks, wide exits and clear gaps that keep letters from crowding. Aaargh is the one to command attention with its uniform joints, but the Mincho carries the quiet detail.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-bona-nova: Bona Nova is an editorial text serif with a restrained swell in its curves and mouths that stay open. Aaargh is best at forceful, uniform-stroke statements, while Bona Nova excels at bookish text with stems a touch heavier than crossbars.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-bona-nova-sc: Bona Nova SC reads refined and classic, its small counters never clogged. The strongest quality is the contrast in temperament: Aaargh's horizontals match its verticals, while the serif lightens gently toward each curve's ends.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-brawler: Aaargh sets a strong, commanding tone with no modulation between its stems and connecting strokes, so nothing feels softened. It excels at force, while Brawler, a text serif, delivers literary refinement through a gentle thick-thin rhythm.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-brygada-1918: Aaargh is a display face built on one line width, whether the stroke curves or runs straight. Brygada 1918, a text serif, does dignified traditional reading best, with medium-range modulation and a wide-open ring of a c.
